'''Michael Roman Wasielewski''' is an American [[Physical chemistry|physical chemist]]. He is currently the Clare Hamilton Hall Professor of [[Chemistry]], Director of the Center for Molecular Quantum Transduction (CMQT), and Director of the Institute for Quantum Information Research and Engineering (INQUIRE) at [[Northwestern University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chemistry.northwestern.edu/people/core-faculty/profiles/michael-wasielewski.html|title=Michael R. Wasielewski: Department of Chemistry - Northwestern University|website=www.chemistry.northwestern.edu|language=en|access-date=2017-04-02}}</ref>

Wasielewski is known for his research on light-driven charge transfer and transport in molecules and materials, [[photosynthesis]], nanoscale materials for solar energy conversion, spin dynamics of multi-spin molecules, molecular materials for [[optoelectronics]] and [[quantum information science]], and [[Time-resolved spectroscopy|time-resolved]] optical and [[Electron paramagnetic resonance|electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy]].

== Education and early life ==
Wasielewski was born on the [[South Side, Chicago|South Side]] of [[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]], and spent his formative years in close proximity to both the [[University of Chicago]] and Chicago's steel making industry. He studied chemistry at University of Chicago under the direction of Leon Stock (B.S. 1971, Ph.D. 1975). His graduate research revealed how the electron-nuclear [[Hyperfine structure|hyperfine splittings]] of [[hydrogen]], [[carbon-13]], and [[fluorine]] atoms depend on the structure of the [[Paramagnetism|paramagnetic]] molecules. After the completion of his Ph.D., Wasielewski studied [[antiaromaticity]] under the direction of [[Ronald Breslow]] at [[Columbia University]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Forbes|first=Malcolm|last2=Hammarstrom|first2=Leif|last3=Vura-Weis|first3=Josh|last4=Weiss|first4=Emily|title=Biography of Michael R. Wasielewski|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry B|language=en|volume=114|issue=45|pages=14112–14116|doi=10.1021/jp106711n|pmid=21070052|year=2010}}</ref>

== The Wasielewski Group ==
Wasielewski joined Northwestern University in 1994. During his time at Northwestern, Wasielewski has collaborated extensively with his colleagues [[Mark Ratner]], [[Tobin J. Marks|Tobin Marks]], Fred Lewis, [[Fraser Stoddart]], and others to study molecular charge transfer and photophysics. Currently, the Wasielewski group is organized into two teams:
* [[Solar energy conversion|Solar Energy Conversion]]
* [[Quantum Information Science]]
